newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik fighters give government 1000 GMT deadline.
newsitem.headline: Tajik fighters give government 1000 GMT deadline.

text.p: Islamic fighters holding more than a dozen Russian and Western hostages gave the Tajik government until 1000 GMT on Friday to meet their demands, a presidential spokesman said.

Zafar Saidov told Reuters that the hostage takers had threatened to take their captives to the mountains and launch a guerrilla war against the government if their demand -- a swap of the hostages for a group of their supporters -- were not met.
The Tajik government had flown 35 supporters of the hostage-takers into Tajikistan from Afghanistan on Thursday. The fighters are led by brothers Bakhram and Rizvon Sadirov.

The brothers want to swap all the hostages for all the fighters and say their supporters must be armed. The government is ready to accept most demands but sticking points appear to be the venue of the swap and the arming of the Sadirovs' fighters.

The hostage crisis started early last week. The armed Islamic group are holding three U.N. observers -- two Swiss and a Ukrainian -- along with four Russian journalists, four staff of the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR and the Tajik security minister, who was seized when he arrived to negotiate.
Bakhram Sadirov told the U.N. mission in the Tajik capital Dushanbe on Friday that his group had shot dead one of the U.N. military observers, but there has been no independent confirmation.
